findings.finding: supervisor.py produces REMEDIATE_PATCH suggested actions without entity_id, causing buildRemediationBody in the SDK to reject them.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/agents/supervisor.py:298: suggested_actions=[{"action": "REMEDIATE_PATCH", "violation_id": v.violation_id, "patch": v.remediation_patch} for v in audit_res.violations if v.remediation_patch]. Running sup.process_message("audit compliance", jurisdiction=Jurisdiction.UAE, auth=auth, context=ctx) outputs action {"action": "REMEDIATE_PATCH", "violation_id": "VIO-PROB-EMP-001", "patch": {"probation_days": 180}} without entity_id. In Node: core.buildRemediationBody(action) returns null.
findings.reproduce: 1. Run python: from hrms_plugin.agents.supervisor import SupervisorAgent; from hrms_plugin.agents.compliance import ComplianceAgent, Jurisdiction; from hrms_plugin.security.rbac import AuthContext, UserRole; res = SupervisorAgent(compliance_agent=ComplianceAgent()).process_message("audit compliance", jurisdiction=Jurisdiction.UAE, auth=AuthContext(tenant_id="tenant_default", user_id="USR-1", roles=[UserRole.HR_ADMIN]), context={"employees": [{"id": "EMP-001", "name": "Test", "probation_days": 200, "jurisdiction": "AE"}]}); 2. Pass res.suggested_actions[0] into core.buildRemediationBody in Node. Observe return value is null and UI emits error message refusing remediation.

findings.finding: The /v1/remediate/execute endpoint called by the SDK does not enforce the server-side two-person approval rule claimed by spec decision D4.
findings.evidence: Spec decision D4 claims: "Approval stays server-side (piece F2 two-person rule)". However, sdk/copilot.js line 358 targets /v1/remediate/execute rather than writeback endpoints. In hrms_plugin/server/app.py:465-493, execute_remediation only checks require(Permission.EXECUTE_REMEDIATION, max_token_age_seconds=REMEDIATION_MAX_TOKEN_AGE_SECONDS); it has no proposer tracking, no separation-of-duties check, and no two-person approval enforcement.
findings.reproduce: Inspect hrms_plugin/server/app.py:465-493. Send POST /v1/remediate/execute with a valid Bearer token possessing EXECUTE_REMEDIATION. The single caller can unilaterally approve and queue remediation without any prior proposer or second-person approval.

findings.finding: Confirmation prompts, describePatch, and error handlers double-escape HTML, causing raw HTML entities to render visibly in the user interface.
findings.evidence: In sdk/copilot.js line 346: appendMessage is passed "Review the change for **${escapeHtml(body.entity_id)}** before approving:\n\n${lines}" where lines is generated by describePatch (line 122) which already calls escapeHtml. In appendMessage line 291: bubble.innerHTML = formatMarkdown(text), which executes escapeHtml on line 30. For input "EMP & 01", output is "Review the change for EMP & 01", rendering "EMP & 01" in the DOM. Lines 365, 368, and 370 also double-escape.
findings.reproduce: In Node: const core = require("./sdk/copilot.js"); const msg = "Review the change for **" + core.escapeHtml("EMP & 01") + "**"; console.log(core.formatMarkdown(msg)); -> outputs "&amp;".

findings.finding: formatMarkdown processes inline code placeholders before links, allowing code blocks in link URLs to inject unescaped HTML tags and quotes into href attributes.
findings.evidence:
In sdk/copilot.js, inline code replacement on line 40 produces "⟦IC0⟧". The link regex on line 48 matches (https:\/\/[^\s)&]+), which consumes "⟦IC0⟧". Line 79 replaces "⟦IC0⟧" with "...". Feeding payload "[x](https://example.com#`code`)" produces: "

code\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" class=\"md-link\">x

". The unescaped quotes in class=\"inline-code\" prematurely close href and break DOM attribute parsing.
findings.reproduce: In Node: const core = require("./sdk/copilot.js"); console.log(core.formatMarkdown("[x](https://example.com#`code`)")); observe unescaped <code class="inline-code"> tag embedded directly inside the href attribute string.

findings.finding: sendMessage and sendVoiceAudio do not check res.ok, resulting in silent failures and empty chat bubbles on HTTP 401 or 500 responses.
findings.evidence:
In sdk/copilot.js lines 267 and 236: const data = await res.json() is called without inspecting res.ok. On 401 Unauthorized or 422 Unprocessable Entity, FastAPI returns {"detail": "..."}. Because data.reply_text is undefined, appendMessage('assistant', undefined) renders an empty bubble (
) without displaying any error to the user.
findings.reproduce: Inspect sdk/copilot.js:256-271. When apiUrl/v1/chat returns HTTP 401 (e.g. invalid or expired token), fetch does not throw; res.json() yields {"detail": "..."}, and appendMessage renders an empty bubble.

findings.finding: buildRemediationBody hardcodes target_entity as EMPLOYEE, failing to accurately target non-employee entity compliance violations.
findings.evidence: In sdk/copilot.js line 117: return { violation_id: action.violation_id, target_entity: 'EMPLOYEE', entity_id: action.entity_id, patch_payload: action.patch }. In hrms_plugin/agents/compliance.py:25, ComplianceViolation specifies entity_type as "EMPLOYEE", "PAYROLL", "PUNCH_LOG", or "LEAVE". A non-employee violation will improperly submit target_entity: 'EMPLOYEE'.
findings.reproduce: Call core.buildRemediationBody({ violation_id: 'V1', entity_id: 'PAY-001', patch: { total: 100 } }); returned object hardcodes target_entity: 'EMPLOYEE'.

findings.finding: buildRemediationBody permits arrays as patches due to typeof [] === 'object', emitting payload types rejected by the backend.
findings.evidence: In sdk/copilot.js line 116: if (!action.patch || typeof action.patch !== 'object') return null. In JavaScript, typeof [] is 'object' and ![] is false. Calling core.buildRemediationBody({ violation_id: 'V1', entity_id: 'E1', patch: [] }) returns an object with patch_payload: []. RemediationExecuteRequest.patch_payload on the server requires Dict[str, Any] and rejects arrays with HTTP 422.
findings.reproduce: In Node: const core = require("./sdk/copilot.js"); console.log(core.buildRemediationBody({ violation_id: 'V1', entity_id: 'E1', patch: [] })); -> returns non-null object with array patch_payload.

findings.finding: XSS test suite contains assertions that pass vacuously for non-link payload vectors.
findings.evidence: In sdk/test/copilot.test.js lines 38-39: assert.doesNotMatch(html, /href="(?!https:\/\/)/i) and assert.doesNotMatch(html, /javascript:[^<]*<\/a>/i) are evaluated against non-link XSS vectors like '' and ''. These assertions pass vacuously because the generated HTML lacks href=" or entirely.
findings.reproduce:
Review sdk/test/copilot.test.js:31-41. For vector '', html is '

<script>alert(1)</script>

'. The assertions checking href=" and javascript:... pass trivially without testing any property of the payload.

findings.finding: Markdown link conversion rejects any HTTPS URL containing an ampersand, breaking legitimate multi-parameter URLs.
findings.evidence: In sdk/copilot.js line 48: the URL capture regex is (https:\/\/[^\s)&]+). Because escapeHtml converts '&' to '&', any markdown URL with multiple query parameters (e.g. '[Docs](https://example.com/api?a=1&b=2)') is rejected by the link regex and rendered as plain text '[Docs](https://example.com/api?a=1&b=2)'.
findings.reproduce:
In Node: const core = require("./sdk/copilot.js"); console.log(core.formatMarkdown("[Docs](https://example.com/api?a=1&b=2)")); -> outputs unlinked paragraph '

[Docs](https://example.com/api?a=1&b=2)

'.
